card.title: Free-body diagram (FBD)
card.body: A sketch that isolates **one chosen object** and draws arrows for **every external force acting on it** (such as $\vec{W}$, $\vec{N}$, $\vec{T}$, $\vec{f}$) before writing $\sum F_x$ and $\sum F_y$.
card.says: include only forces **on** the object—never draw forces the object exerts on other things, and never draw $m\vec{a}$ as an extra force arrow.
card.from: standard mechanics problem-solving practice built on Newton's laws: turning a word problem into clean axis-by-axis equations.
card.useWhen: solving **any** force, friction, pulley, elevator, or inclined-plane problem—always draw the FBD first before picking formulas.
card.example: A $5\text{ kg}$ crate on a flat floor ($g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$) pulled horizontally right by a rope with $40\text{ N}$ while $f_k = 15\text{ N}$ has 4 arrows: $W = 49\text{ N}$ down, $N = 49\text{ N}$ up, $T = 40\text{ N}$ right, $f_k = 15\text{ N}$ left → $\sum F_x = 40 - 15 = 25\text{ N}$, so $a_x = \dfrac{25}{5} = 5\text{ m/s}^2$.
card.analogy: A bank statement for one account: list only deposits and withdrawals on that account, ignoring transfers happening between other people.
